### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every trace contained exactly one of five alternative activities: A18 in about 27 of 100 traces, A17 in about 25, A20 in about 19, A14 in about 17 and A19 in about 14. These shares sum to all traces, and no tested pair of them ever occurred in the same trace. [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, REL003, REL029, REL044]
- In the earlier window, A43 fed this choice — its outgoing transitions went to A18 (about 27%), A17 (about 25%), A20 (about 19%), A14 (about 17%) and A19 (about 13%) — and each of the five activities led only on to A28, which it preceded. [DIR001, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR011, REL036, REL042, REL043]
- In the later window, A14, A17, A18, A19 and A20 appear in no trace at all (0 of 200), while A15, A16, A25, A26 and A27 each appear in every trace (200 of 200). [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC002, OCC003, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]
- In the later window, A43 leads into this new group (outgoing transitions to A15 about 25%, A26 about 21%, A27 about 20%, A16 about 18%, A25 about 17%) and precedes each of the five in every trace. [DIR011, REL019, REL028, REL054, REL057, REL059]
- The five new activities all run within the same trace but without a fixed order between them: for example A15 precedes A16 in about 52 of 100 traces and A16 precedes A15 in about 48, and the other pairs show similarly even splits. [REL010, REL015, REL024, REL051, REL052, REL055]
- Each of the new activities precedes A28 in every trace, and each also connects directly to the other four members of the group as well as to A28. [REL018, REL027, REL053, REL056, REL058, DIR002, DIR003, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010]
- A28 is present in all traces in both windows but sits later in the later window (mean relative position about 0.39 versus 0.47), while A43 sits slightly earlier (about 0.32 versus 0.29); these are event positions, not clock times. [POS011, POS012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the segment between A43 and A28 was restructured: the earlier exclusive branch, in which A43 was followed by exactly one of A14, A17, A18, A19 or A20 and that single activity led to A28, was replaced in the later window by a block in which A43 is followed by all five of A15, A16, A25, A26 and A27 in every trace, executed in no fixed order among themselves, before A28. This is shown directly and consistently: participation moved from mutually exclusive minorities (about 14–27 in 100 traces each) to all traces for the new five and none for the old five; A43's outgoing transitions switched entirely from the old set to the new set; the co-occurrence and ordering relations show the new block; and A28's later position is consistent with a larger set of activities now preceding it. Because the old activities are wholly absent later and the new ones wholly absent earlier, this is a replacement of one path by another, not a shift in how often existing paths are taken. Screening also qualifies 92 control-flow items where fewer than 1 would be expected if nothing had changed, so the pattern as a whole cannot be attributed to random sampling, and every item's difference exceeds essentially all random re-splits of the pooled data (empirical strength about 99.5 in 100). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, DIR011, REL019, REL035, REL053, POS011, screening]

Limitations: the evidence cannot rule out that the new activities are relabelled counterparts of the old ones rather than genuinely different work, since the activity codes are anonymous; and the mixed orders show only that no fixed ordering constraint exists between the five new activities, not that they execute in parallel. [REL010, REL015, REL051]
